newsitem.title: USA: Travelers to buy BankAmerica unit.
newsitem.headline: Travelers to buy BankAmerica unit.

text.p: Travelers Group Inc's Commercial Credit Co said Monday it had agreed to buy Security Pacific Financial Services, BankAmerica Corp's consumer finance subsidiary, for $1.6 billion.

Commercial Credit said the price represents a premium of about $300 million over the BankAmerica unit's net tangible assets, which include about $1.2 billion of consumer finance receivables and $70 million of other assets.
BankAmerica said the transaction will result in capital for reinvestment in other BankAamerica businesses of $280 million.
BankAmerica said in March that it planned to sell Security Pacific Financial.

"This transaction is strategically important to us," said Commercial Credit Chief Executive Robdrt Willumstad, "as it establishes our position as the third largest independent consumer finance company in the U.S. and will enable us to expand our management pool with talented people whose culture and work ethic are compatible with our own."
Commercial Credit said financing for the deal will consist of a Travelers Group equity contribution of about $500 million. Commercial Credit will finance the remainder with debt.
Commercial Credit said its "leverage ratios will remain very conservative relative to its industry, even after the transaction."
The transaction is subject to approval by various regulatory agencies. It is expected to be completed during the third quarter, Commercial Credit said.

Security Pacific Financial Services, with 297 branch offices, provides home equity and other real estate-secured loans, as well as unsecured loans and sales financing through retail merchants. It became part of BankAmerica in 1992 when the bank holding company acquired Security Pacific Corp.
Commercial Credit is a consumer lending company based in Baltimore. It has 859 offices in 44 states and more than $8.5 billion in receivables.
